project.name: Prunus Mume - Core Learning Experience
project.instruction: Continue from the current project. Do not create a new project, redesign the product, or replace the existing home page.

currentState: The project uses Next.js App Router, React, TypeScript, and the existing global CSS.
Only the home route is currently implemented.
Question bank search, daily sign-in, learning progress, and other home-page interactions currently use local mock data.
The existing home page defines the Meiwen brand and must be treated as the design system for all new pages.

designSystem.productType: Chinese end-user education and question-bank application, not an admin dashboard
principles: Use generous whitespace, a near-white light-gray background, white cards, thin borders, and restrained shadows.
Use the existing plum or burgundy variables as the primary brand color.
Use deep burgundy for VIP surfaces and green only for completed or successful states.

Continue the current large headings, tight heading letter spacing, restrained body typography, 18-28px corner radii, pill tags, linear progress bars, circular progress indicators, and abstract question-bank covers.
Reuse the CSS variables and component appearance already defined in app/globals.css.
Do not introduce a second component library or an unrelated visual system.
Avoid excessive gradients, glassmorphism, colorful icon sets, oversized shadows, and dense dashboard layouts.
Preserve the existing home-page copy, primary layout, and visual appearance. Only make changes required for shared components and real navigation.

objective: Complete the core journey from discovering a question bank to browsing questions and practicing a question, while making all relevant home-page entry points functional.

routes.name: Login
requirements: Create a branded login page with account and password fields.
Include password visibility, remember-session control, login action, and a registration link.
Design normal, validation-error, and submitting states.

routes.name: Register
requirements: Include account, password, password confirmation, terms acceptance, registration action, and a return-to-login link.
Design normal, validation-error, and submitting states.

routes.name: Question Bank List
requirements: Provide search, sorting, category or difficulty filters, result count, question-bank cards, pagination, and an empty state.
Use either a grid or list layout that naturally extends the home-page question-bank cards.

routes.name: Question Bank Detail
requirements: Show the cover, title, description, creator, question count, and learning progress.
Show a paginated question list with difficulty, tags, view count, like count, favourite count, and VIP status.

routes.name: Question Search
requirements: Support keyword, tag, difficulty, and question-bank filtering.
Provide a desktop filter area and a mobile-friendly filter drawer or sheet.
Include result count, pagination, loading, empty, and error states.

routes.name: Question Detail and Practice
requirements: Clearly present the question content, tags, difficulty, and source question bank.
Keep the answer collapsed until the user selects Show Answer.
Allow like and favourite toggling with immediate mock count updates.
For a VIP question viewed by a non-member, hide the answer and show a restrained upgrade card linking to /membership.
Provide previous-question, next-question, and return-to-bank actions.

globalNavigation: Extract the current home-page navigation into a reusable site Header without changing its desktop appearance.
Desktop navigation must include Home, Question Banks, and All Questions.
My Favourites and the avatar must navigate to their corresponding pages.
The current layout hides primary navigation below 780px. Add a usable mobile navigation pattern, such as a restrained bottom navigation or menu drawer.
Show a clear active state for the current route.
implementationConstraints: Focus on a complete, navigable, high-fidelity frontend in this stage. Do not connect to the real backend yet.
Use structured mock data and TypeScript types instead of embedding large data objects directly in JSX.
Search, filtering, pagination, answer reveal, likes, favourites, and VIP gating must be genuinely interactive.
Use real application routes. Do not keep placeholder href="#" navigation.
Provide loading, empty, and error states that match the existing visual language.
Support desktop, tablet, and approximately 390px mobile widths without horizontal scrolling.
Maintain keyboard accessibility, visible focus states, semantic heading order, and appropriate ARIA labels.
Preserve existing data-od-id attributes and add stable data-od-id attributes to important new elements.
Update or replace stale starter tests when necessary. Do not restore the old starter loading skeleton merely to satisfy outdated tests.
acceptanceCriteria: The existing home page remains visually consistent while its core entry points become functional.
All six routes can be opened directly and survive a browser refresh.
A user can navigate from the home page to a bank list, bank detail, and question detail, then reveal an answer and toggle like or favourite state.
A non-member cannot see the answer of a VIP question and receives an upgrade path instead.
Desktop and mobile both provide complete navigation.
The project passes TypeScript, lint, and build checks.
